- When sentiment turns sharply positive (e.g., +1.00) followed by a spike in price, model tends to overreact and overshoot — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a strong negative sentiment shift (e.g., -0.33 to -1.00), model often underreacts — adjust downward by 3–7% to match true mean reversion.
- If sentiment change is flat or neutral (e.g., ±0.33) over 3–5 days, model overfits recent noise — smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.
- When news volume is low (0.0) and sentiment is volatile, model overestimates volatility — dampen forecast by 2–5% to reflect reduced information.
- If model forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply downward bias correction — subtract 3–5% from next forecast if sentiment remains neutral or mildly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong upward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive +0.67) and price is rising, model often fails to anticipate mean reversion — cap forecast at 10–15% below recent peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate short-term volatility — apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce noise in forecast tail.
